goal: Feed an anaerobic digester with two pumps so that its net methane over the first 100 days is as high as possible and no episode fails. The score of an episode is net_methane (m3/d): the mean true methane outflow minus 0.395 times the mean true outflow of organic acids over decisions 1 to 400. An episode fails when the digester collapses (true pH below 6.0 at the end of any of its 568 decisions, the run-out included) or does not run to its end. A program with no failed episode ranks above every program with one, whatever their scores. The goal is the highest mean score over the evaluation episodes with no failed episode.
description:
The task loading of microbesGYM's environment a1_adm1, wrapped unchanged: the benchmark's own episode gives the readings and computes the score. The numbers below are from the task's description (TASK.md) and from the nominal model of the task.

THE DIGESTER. A closed, stirred tank with 3400 m3 of liquid and 300 m3 of gas at 35 C, modelled with ADM1 (the version of the Benchmark Simulation Model no. 2). Microorganisms turn the feed into methane in stages. Solid carbohydrates, proteins and lipids are hydrolysed (10 per day), sugars, amino acids and fatty acids are taken up fast and become the organic acids valerate, butyrate, propionate and acetate, and two groups of methanogens make methane from acetate and from hydrogen. The methanogens that use acetate are the slow step: they grow at most 0.4 per day, they are inhibited by free ammonia, and they work at half their rate at pH 6.5 and at about 3 % of it at pH 6.0. Too much feed therefore makes acids faster than they are used, the pH falls, the methanogens slow down and the acids rise further. The digester then collapses: the pH settles near 4, the methane stops and the acids leave with the liquid. Every group needs inorganic nitrogen to grow. The liquid that leaves always equals the feeds together, so the volume stays constant and all liquid that enters also washes microorganisms out.

ACTION: a list of two floats, [sludge_rate, carbohydrate_rate], the rates that the program asks for, in m3/d. sludge_rate is from 0 to 1000 and changes by at most 34 per decision; it starts at 85. carbohydrate_rate is from 0 to 300 and changes by at most 10 per decision; it starts at 0. An action outside these limits is rejected and ends the episode as a failure of the program. A change larger than the limit is cut to it, so each pump needs 30 decisions to cross its range. One decision every 6 hours.

THE THREE FEEDS. (1) The sludge pump delivers sludge: per m3 5 kgCOD carbohydrates, 20 proteins, 5 lipids, 2 mixed organic matter, 25 inert solids, and inorganic carbon, inorganic nitrogen and dissolved salts, which buffer the pH. (2) The carbohydrate pump delivers a concentrate of 200 kgCOD of solid carbohydrates per m3 in water, about six times the degradable matter of sludge, with no nitrogen and no buffer. It is what makes much methane, and too much of it makes the digester collapse. Too much sludge collapses it too, by washing the microorganisms out. (3) A third feed of sludge that no program sets follows a schedule that is the same in every episode: 63 to 148 m3/d, mean 84, changing every 6 hours. On two days of every week it is more dilute (0.9 times the concentrations), and once in an episode, on days 50 and 51, a storm brings 116 to 148 m3/d at 0.65 times the concentrations. A program is not told the schedule and has no clock.

WHAT DIFFERS BETWEEN EPISODES. The seed draws the carbohydrates, proteins and lipids of each of the three sludge recipes, each between 0.7 and 1.4 times nominal and constant within the episode, and the errors of the sensors. How much feed a digester bears depends on its sludge, which is never observed.

OBSERVABLES. Every reading has a random error with the standard deviation given; no sensor has an offset. At every decision, without delay: ch4_flow and co2_flow (gas meters, m3/d, 2 % of the value), ch4_pressure (partial pressure of methane, bar, 0.01 bar), ph (probe, 0.1 pH, so a single reading says little and readings must be combined). Laboratory values, sampled at every 4th decision and arriving 4 decisions later, all five together: vfa_s_va, vfa_s_bu, vfa_s_pro, vfa_s_ac (valerate, butyrate, propionate, acetate, kgCOD per litre, 5 %; multiply by 1000 for kgCOD/m3) and inorganic_carbon (mM, 5 %). They are None during the first day, and afterwards the newest value is 4 to 7 decisions old. lab_age is that age in decisions, None before the first arrives; it is 4 at the decision at which new values arrive. sludge_rate and carbohydrate_rate are the rates at which the pumps stand now, after the limit on their change. The gas meters report a volume at the pressure of the gas above the liquid, which rises with the production (5.5 % above atmospheric at the start, 29 % with the pumps at 200 and 100), so the methane of the score, counted at atmospheric pressure, is higher than ch4_flow by that ratio. Not observed: the day, the number of decisions, the seed, the microorganisms, the nitrogen, the sludge of the episode and every true value.

EPISODE. 568 decisions (142 days). Every episode starts from the same steady state, about 1800 m3/d of methane. Decisions 1 to 400 (100 days) are scored. Decisions 401 to 568 are the run-out: the program keeps running exactly as before, nothing there adds to the score, but a collapse there fails the episode. Nothing ends an episode early; a collapsed digester stays in it and its negative net methane is counted.

SCORE AND EPISODE RECORD. These keys are None at every step and are filled in only in the observation that ends the episode, which no program acts on. They are computed from the true state. net_methane = the score, m3/d: mean methane outflow minus 0.395 times the mean outflow of the four acids (kgCOD/d) over decisions 1 to 400. net_methane_start, net_methane_middle, net_methane_end = the same over decisions 1 to 80, 81 to 240 and 241 to 400, so the score is 0.2 x start + 0.4 x middle + 0.4 x end. net_methane_run_out = the same over decisions 401 to 568, not in the score; a program that holds what it reached shows a run-out equal to its end phase. collapsed = 1 if the true pH was below 6.0 at the end of any decision, else 0. failed = True if the digester collapsed or the episode did not run all 568 decisions. mean_ch4_flow and mean_acids_out = the two parts of the score. min_ph and max_total_vfa (kgCOD/m3) = extremes over all 568 decisions. end_ph and end_total_vfa = the state after the last decision. REWARD of a step: the true net methane of that decision, m3/d, at every decision including the run-out; a program never sees it.

WHAT PROGRAMS THAT READ NO SENSOR SHOW. All numbers are means of net methane (m3/d) over the 20 training episodes of the seeds 6001 to 6020, unless another number of episodes is given. The baseline of this setup plays the four programs marked with a star.

Fixed rates: both pumps move as fast as their limits allow and are then held. Pumps left at 85 and 0: 1760, no collapse, lowest pH 7.35. To 200 and 100 (hold_200_100, star): 9330, no collapse, lowest pH 6.67. To 200 and 110: 3890, with 7 of 20 collapsed on day 6 or 7; the 13 others made 9700.

Both pumps rising together: ramp_S_C_step raises the carbohydrate pump by step m3/d per decision to C and the sludge pump in proportion from 85 to S, and then holds both. To 300 and 130 at step 10, as fast as allowed: all 20 collapsed. At step 3, in 11 days (ramp_300_130_3, star): 11658, no collapse, lowest pH 6.61, start phase 9161 and 12280 afterwards; on the 80 evaluation episodes of this setup the same program lost one digester, late in the episode. At step 1, in 33 days: 10572, no collapse, start phase 4985. To 400 and 130 at step 3: 11 of 20 collapsed. To 400 and 150 at step 3: 13 of 20 collapsed. To 480 and 172 at step 1, in 43 days: 8 of 20 collapsed, the 12 others made 13451 with a start phase of 5360.

A start without sludge: start_F_S_C first lowers the sludge pump to 0, where it is after 3 decisions, and raises the concentrate by 5.5 m3/d per decision to F = 110 m3/d in 5 days. Then it raises the sludge by 5 to 8 m3/d per decision and the concentrate slowly to S and C, which both reach about 14 days later, and holds them. To 400 and 130 (start_110_400_130, star): 12289, no collapse, scores from 11436 to 13180, start phase 9228 and 13050 afterwards. On the 80 evaluation episodes of this setup the same program scored 12209 with no collapse and a lowest pH of 6.69. So the rates 400 and 130, which collapsed 11 of 20 digesters when both pumps rose together, held in all 100 digesters after a start without sludge. To 300 and 130: 11597, no collapse. To 480 and 150: 5 of 20 collapsed, between day 21 and day 54, and the 15 others made 13974. To 450 and 150 with the concentrate first raised by 6.5 per decision to 130: 4 of 20 collapsed, and the 16 others made 13956 with a start phase of 10540. To 480 and 172 (start_110_480_172, star): 8 of 20 collapsed, all between day 18 and day 20, and the 12 others made 15345, from 14455 to 15959, with a start phase of 10550 and 16540 in the middle and in the end phase.

The readings during a start without sludge, as means over the 20 digesters under start_110_400_130: the methane flow rose from 1800 m3/d to 3500 on day 3, 5500 on day 5 and 7200 on day 8. The acids (the sum of the four, kgCOD/m3) rose from 0.25 to 0.8 on day 5 and 1.2 on day 8, and were back at 0.5 on day 10 and 0.35 on day 13, while the sludge pump was rising by 7 m3/d per decision. The pH fell from 7.43 to 7.10 on day 5 and 7.0 on day 10. From day 20 on, with the pumps at 400 and 130, the digesters held a methane flow near 9600, acids of 0.5 to 0.6, an inorganic carbon near 87 mM and a pH near 6.9.

What this shows. (1) The start decides, and it is the sludge pump that endangers it. With the sludge pump at 0 the liquid of the tank is replaced by the third feed and the concentrate alone, about 190 m3/d in place of 500, so the likely reason is that the microorganisms multiply on the concentrate faster than they are washed out. A digester then bears within 5 days a rate of concentrate that collapses it when the sludge rises with it, and it bears much sludge afterwards. Every day at a low load is lost score, and the start phase is a fifth of the score. No program here has tried, with the sludge pump at 0, a faster rise of the concentrate than 6.5 m3/d per decision or a higher first rate than 130, and none has brought the sludge back faster than by 8 m3/d per decision; the limits of the pumps allow 10 and 34. None has set the moment at which the sludge comes back by a reading.

(2) Digesters differ, and a fixed plan must stay below what the weakest bears. The methane flow before the pumps move tells them apart roughly: with the pumps at 85 and 0, ch4_flow is between 1400 and 2100 m3/d, depending on the sludge of the episode. What a digester holds under a known load tells them apart exactly. At 400 and 130, the 20 digesters ended at a pH between 6.72 and 7.05. The 8 that ended at 6.72 to 6.80 all collapsed at 480 and 172, and their starting flows were below 1670. The 12 that ended at 6.87 to 7.05 all bore 480 and 172, where their lowest pH was 6.70 to 6.91, so the richest of them had room for more. Nothing here shows how much more: no program has loaded a digester beyond 480 and 172.

(3) The readings tell the two kinds apart days before a collapse. Under start_110_480_172, the 8 digesters that collapsed and the 12 that did not had the same pump rates at every decision. Their mean pH readings were 6.94 against 7.02 on day 10, 6.83 against 6.92 on day 13 and 6.73 against 6.88 on day 16. Their inorganic carbon was 104 against 111 mM on day 10, 86 against 99 on day 13 and 74 against 91 on day 16. Their acids were alike and low, 0.4 to 0.5 kgCOD/m3, until the collapse on days 18 to 20, so the acids gave no warning of it. A single pH reading has an error of 0.1, so such differences show only in an average of many readings.

(4) So no pair of rates and no timetable is right for every digester. A program that reads during the episode what its own digester bears, and sets its rates by that, can load each digester to its own limit, where a fixed plan loses either the weak digesters or the methane of the strong ones.

WHAT THE SENSORS SHOW ON THE WAY TO A COLLAPSE. There are two ways to collapse, and different readings announce them. The values are means of the readings as a program gets them, over one or two days. (a) Overload by speed: a rich digester (seed 6013) under ramp_400_150_3. Acetate (vfa_s_ac x 1000) rose with every laboratory result: 0.2 on day 1, 0.8 on day 3, 1.8 on day 5, 2.7 on day 7, 3.6 on day 9 and 3.8 on day 11. The inorganic carbon fell from 152 to 73 mM and the pH from 7.5 to 6.7 on day 11. Over day 12 the pH readings averaged 5.6 and the methane flow fell by more than half; a day later the methane had stopped, and the acids went on to 35. The same digester under ramp_480_172_1: acetate stayed below 1.25 and settled at 0.8, the inorganic carbon settled at 90 and the pH at 6.87, with a methane flow of 12000. (b) Loss of buffer: a lean digester (seed 6001) under ramp_480_172_1. The acids stayed between 0.4 and 0.6 until the end and gave no warning. The inorganic carbon fell steadily as the load rose: 152 mM on day 1, 124 on day 9, 107 on day 17, 85 on day 25, 64 on day 33 and 55 on day 41. The pH fell with it: 7.45 at the start, 7.26 around day 9, 7.08 around day 17, 6.89 around day 26 and 6.74 over days 32 to 40. The digester collapsed between day 41 and day 45, just after the pumps had reached 480 and 172. The same digester under ramp_300_130_3 settled at an inorganic carbon of 58 and a pH of 6.67 and did not collapse. So rising acetate announces an overload by speed days ahead, and falling inorganic carbon and pH announce a loss of buffer weeks ahead. The concentrate brings no buffer and the sludge does. In every surviving episode of these programs the lowest true pH was 6.59 or higher, and in every collapsed one it was between 4.0 and 4.4: there was nothing in between.

A collapse comes fast and cannot be undone: the pH was still at or above 6.5 three decisions before it was below 6.0, and closing or lowering the pumps once the true pH was below 6.5 brought no digester back. Feeding more than a digester bears for good can pay inside the scored days and collapse later, on day 118 or 134 in trials; the run-out counts such a collapse.

WHAT EARLIER PROGRAMS OF THIS LOOP SHOWED. Programs with feedback that settled at 210 to 270 m3/d of sludge and 90 to 112 of concentrate scored 10000 to 11100, which is below start_110_400_130, a program that reads no sensor. Programs that then raised both pumps quickly toward higher rates collapsed in most episodes. All of them raised the sludge pump from the first decision on: none lowered it at the start, and none set its load by what its own digester showed.

WHAT THE DESIGNER OF THE TASK'S OWN FEEDBACK CONTROLLER WAS HANDED. The benchmark has a controller of two PI loops, and its record says what a person chose for it before any search. A program of this loop may use the same knowledge. The pairing: the carbohydrate pump follows the pH, and the sludge pump follows the sum of the four acids. The reason given: the concentrate is the feed that sours the digester, and the pH shows it within hours, so the fast measurement steers the dangerous feed; the sludge sets how long the liquid stays in the digester, which decides how much of the acids becomes methane before the liquid leaves, so the acids steer the sludge. The directions: the carbohydrate pump goes up when the pH is above its setpoint and down when it is below; the sludge pump goes down when the acids are above their setpoint and up when they are below. A loop computes, at each new measurement, error = smoothed measured value - setpoint and output = start + gain x (error + integral / integral time), where the integral adds up error x hours since the measurement before and is left as it is while the pump has not reached the last output and the error pushes it further away. The smoothed value moves toward each new measurement by the share 1 - exp(-hours / filter time). The ranges in which its ten numbers were searched: pH setpoint 6.7 to 7.6; pH gain 30 to 3000 m3/d per pH unit; pH integral time 6 to 480 hours; pH filter time 0 to 72 hours; start of the carbohydrate pump 0 to 300 m3/d; acids setpoint 0.06 to 9 kgCOD/m3; acids gain 10 to 1000 m3/d per kgCOD/m3, downward; acids integral time 24 to 480 hours; acids filter time 0 to 144 hours; start of the sludge pump 0 to 1000 m3/d. That controller reads the pH and the four acids and not the gas meters or the inorganic carbon, and it has no safety rule beside its pH loop. Which values its search found, and what it scored, is not shown here.

RULES FOR A PROGRAM. The benchmark gives a controller no clock, and a program is a controller. The rules of this setup say what that means, and an attempt that breaks one is barred whatever its score.

SEEDS. Every episode of the loop is a training episode of the benchmark. Results of other controllers on this task, and the settings that their searches found, are not shown here and are not targets. Set each new milestone above what this loop's own best program reaches, with no failed episode, and keep raising it.

rules.name: no_clock
rules.text: The program keeps no clock of its own. It does not count its calls of act, the decisions, the days or the laboratory results that have arrived, and it does not add up time, in its memory or anywhere else. Nothing that it does may depend on a value that only tells how far the episode has run, because the task gives a controller no clock: with the length of an episode, a count would tell how many scored decisions are left. What a program keeps from one decision to the next is about the digester, for example earlier readings, averages and trends of them or the sum of its control errors, or about what it has done, for example the rates it asked for or a flag that a phase of its own has ended. A list of the last readings with a fixed largest length is allowed. A list or a number that grows with every decision whatever the digester does is a count and breaks the rule.

rules.name: own_memory
rules.text: The program keeps everything that it remembers in the memory dict that act receives. It keeps nothing in a variable of a module that it changes, in a default argument, in an attribute of a function, in a file or anywhere else outside that dict, so that no episode can learn from another one. Constants of a module that are never changed are allowed.

rules.name: observation_only
rules.text: The observation that act receives is the program's only source about the episode. The program reads no file, no environment variable and no clock of the computer, and it draws no random number, so the same readings always give the same actions. It imports nothing of microbesGYM (mgym_engine, mgym_bench), nothing of the plugin (a1_adm1, bridge) and nothing of soft_control_loop except what a skill of the library needs, and it simulates no model of the digester with a solver.

milestones.name: hold
milestones.description: No evaluation episode failed, and the mean score (net_methane, m3/d) over the evaluation episodes is at least 9277. This is what the fixed rates 200 and 100 m3/d (hold_200_100) scored on the evaluation seeds (9277.5, with no failed episode), so the mark asks for a program that does at least as well. The batch check check_hold in the checks file tests it.
